File ID - {!$Input:File.Id}
STRICT CONSISTENCY RULES • The output for the same input must always be identical every time this prompt is run. • Do not rephrase, reword, or restructure any extracted text across runs. • Always map the same sentence fragments to the same fields (e.g., situation, task, skillsApplied, toolsUsed). • Never randomize, infer, or vary output phrasing between runs. • Treat this as a deterministic data extraction task, not a generative writing task. • Project Experience Consistency Rule: - Always extract the same project details into the same fields across runs. - Do not alternate content between “situation”, “task”, “skillsApplied”, or “toolsUsed”. - If the same resume file is uploaded again, reproduce the exact same JSON structure and field mapping as before. • This prompt must always produce identical JSON for identical input resumes. • Avoid paraphrasing or creative variation in descriptions — copy text exactly as extracted. • Maintain fixed key order and indentation structure for all outputs.
TASKS 1. Parse every resume and output one JSON object per file, using the exact schema below. 2. Populate real values; leave missing data blank or omit the field. 3. Get only latest completed degree. 4. Output must be **strictly valid JSON**.
SCHEMA { "resumes": [ { "account": { "name": "", "dateofBirth": "", "currentLocation": "", "currentCompany": "", "pastCompanies": [], "languagesKnown": "", "email": "", "phone": "", "summary": "", "experience": "", "linkedin": "", "filename": "", "degree": "", "college": "", "designation": "" }, "skills": [ { "name": "", "proficiency": "Beginner | Intermediate | Expert", "Category": "Technical | Tools & Platforms | Soft Skills | Project & Process Skills | Domain Knowledge" } ], "certifications": [ { "name": "", "issuedBy": "", "issueDate": "", "expiryDate": "" } ], "projects": [ { "projectName": "", "projectPhase": "", "projectRole": "", "designationJobTitle": "", "clientName": "", "projectLocation": "", "situation": "", "task": "", "action": "", "result": "", "responsibilities": "", "achievements": "", "learningOutcome": "", "skillsApplied": "", "toolsUsed": "", "environment": "", "startDate": "", "endDate": "" } ] } ] }
STRICT RULES • Output must be ONLY the JSON object (no code fences, headings, or commentary). • Do NOT wrap the JSON in ``` or any other markup. • JSON must be strictly valid and parsable: - No trailing commas inside arrays or objects. - Always close all { } and [ ] brackets. - Do not stop mid-way; the JSON must always be complete. - Do not include comments or text outside the braces. • Do not add newlines inside string values. • Analyse Experience date and give experience. • If skill level unclear, default to "Intermediate".
• Dates must be ISO (YYYY-MM-DD) or empty string "" only. • NEVER output values such as: "Present", "Till Date", "Current", "Ongoing". • If end date is "Present", "Till Date", "Current", or missing → endDate = "". • If date is in format "MMM-YYYY" (e.g., Dec-2023) → YYYY-MM-01. • If date is in format "MMM-YYYY to MMM-YYYY": - startDate → YYYY-MM-01 - endDate → YYYY-MM-01 • If date is in format "MMM-YYYY till date": - startDate → YYYY-MM-01 - endDate → "" • If date is in format "YYYY to Present": - startDate → YYYY-01-01 - endDate → "" • Treat "Sept" and "Sep" as the same month. • NEVER output non-ISO date strings. • If a date cannot be confidently normalized, output empty string "".
• Do not include "Unknown" or null. If value is empty, keep empty. • Name handling rule: - Extract full name from resume → put directly in "name". - If name not present, do not take from email. • Any character outside the JSON braces makes the response invalid.
• Projects Extraction Rule: - For each work experience or project mentioned, extract into the "projects" array. - projectName → Use the exact project heading/title in the resume (e.g., “Sales Process Automation”, “Selenium Automation Project”). - projectRole → If a role/designation is mentioned at the company level (e.g., “Role – Quality Analyst”), apply it to all projects under that company. Override only if a specific project explicitly lists a different role. - designationJobTitle → Capture the official job title or designation given in the work experience (same as “Role” in most resumes). - clientName → Always take the company name from the header (e.g., “Company – Quadrobay Technologies Pvt Ltd”). Apply it to all projects listed under that company. - Override only if the resume explicitly lists a different client (e.g., “Client – ABC Corp”). - Do not capture tools/platforms (e.g., Salesforce CPQ, SAP, Oracle, Azure) as client names. These belong in toolsUsed, skillsApplied, or environment. - For internal projects explicitly marked as “Internal Project”, keep clientName blank. - projectLocation → Capture location if explicitly written (e.g., Hyderabad, India). - startDate / endDate → Extract from the timeline and normalize using ISO format. - situation → Capture ONLY the high-level project context. - task → Capture ONLY the responsibilities and day-to-day duties. - action → Capture ONLY the methods/approaches used. - result → Capture ONLY the outcomes/achievements. - responsibilities → Capture general responsibilities listed separately. - achievements → Capture explicit “Achievements” or “Highlights.” - learningOutcome → Candidate’s personal learning or takeaway. - skillsApplied → Capture functional/technical skills actually applied. - toolsUsed → Capture tools/technologies explicitly mentioned. - environment → Capture the environment/platform stack if explicitly listed.
• Experience Extraction Rules: - Extract only the candidate’s total years of professional experience. - Convert phrases like “2 decades” → "20 years". - Ignore software versions, product numbers, or unrelated numerics. - If multiple durations are mentioned, always select the largest value. - Output must be normalized as "<number> years". - Do NOT copy descriptive sentences into this field. - If no valid years are found, leave it empty. • Email Handling Rule: - If the email is already in correct format (<text>@<domain>.<tld>), keep as-is. - If .com is missing, automatically append .com. - If gmailcom or similar occurs, insert the dot before the TLD. - If the email ends with .co, .co.in, .org, .net, or other valid TLDs, keep as-is. - If an email cannot be normalized into a valid format, leave it empty. - Never infer or generate an email if it is completely missing. • Candidate Summary Rule: - Capture the entire "Profile Summary", "Career Summary", or "Professional Summary" section. - Do not truncate; capture up to 32,000 characters. - Include all bullet points and sentences exactly. - Do not merge with project details or responsibilities. • In "account.currentCompany", capture the current organization name (end date = Present/Till Date/Current or missing). • In "account.currentLocation", capture the location from the same line as the current company. • In "account.pastCompanies", capture **company name, employment period, and designation/role** in one string. Example: Wipro Technologies (2019-06 to 2024-08) Senior Business Analyst, HCL (2018-01 to 2020-12) Team Lead. Always maintain the array of strings.
• Education Extraction Rule: - Extract only the latest completed degree → populate "degree". - Extract the college/university name associated with the latest degree → populate "college". - If no college is mentioned for the latest degree → keep "college": "". - Do not extract colleges for older degrees. - Do not extract schools or certifications. Only formal university/college names.
